channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Safety of high-powered sub-ohm devices (part I)
item.description: Power, temperature and device design are often discussed as if they automatically translate into higher danger. With sub-ohm vaping, the more important question is what the evidence actually shows about emissions, exposure and real-world use. High-powered devices should be assessed carefully, but not through assumptions that ignore how experienced users control settings, airflow and liquid consumption. Safety debates need measurements, context and comparison with the risks of continued smoking. (Published on July 27, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: South Africa Tobacco Regulation: The Case for Proportionate Risk
item.description: A regulation that treats every nicotine product as equally dangerous starts from the wrong premise. South Africa’s tobacco policy should recognise that the greatest harm comes from combustion, not nicotine itself. Risk-proportionate regulation would still control access, protect young people and set product standards, but it would not make lower-risk alternatives harder to use than cigarettes. The aim should be to move smokers down the risk continuum, not trap them at the most harmful end. (Published on July 27, 2026bytobaccoharmreduction.net)

item.title: Op-Ed: No air conditioning, but Brussels wants to ban Zyn
item.description: Heat is no longer an abstract climate issue when people are trying to sleep, work or stay safe in homes built for a cooler past. The air-conditioning debate shows how quickly adaptation becomes political: some see cooling as wasteful, others as basic protection against extreme heat. A serious response should not shame people for needing relief, but make cooling cleaner, more efficient and more accessible. Climate policy has to help people live with the risks already here, not only argue about the emissions still to come. (Published on July 27, 2026byyahoo.com)
